english: Let $y=y(x)$, $x>10$, be the solution of the differential equation
with $y(15)=20$. If $\alpha>10$ is such that $y(\alpha)=\dfrac{21}{2}$, then the value of $\alpha$ is ______.
hindi: का वह हल है जिसके लिए $y(15)=20$ है। यदि $\alpha>10$ इस प्रकार है कि $y(\alpha)=\dfrac{21}{2}$, तो $\alpha$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Polar idea: $x\,dx+y\,dy=r\,dr$ with $r=\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}$, so the equation is $r\,dr=r(dx+dy)$
solution_full: In polar form $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$, we have $x\,dx+y\,dy=\dfrac12d\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)=r\,dr$. So the equation becomes $r\,dr=r\,(dx+dy)$, and since $r>0$, $dr=dx+dy$.

Square: $x^{2}+y^{2}=x^{2}+y^{2}+100+2xy-20x-20y$, so $xy-10x-10y+50=0$, that is, $(x-10)(y-10)=50$. (The distance from the origin is $\sqrt2$ times the distance from the line $x+y=10$, so the curve is a hyperbola.)
On $x>10$ the solution is $y=10+\dfrac{50}{x-10}$; at $x=15$ it gives $20$, as required.
originality_note: New: a differential equation that in polar terms says dr = dx + dy, so the solution is a focus-directrix curve with eccentricity sqrt 2 (a rectangular hyperbola (x-10)(y-10) = 50) (way 4). Closest known: x dx + y dy = sqrt(x^2+y^2) dx type exercises (parabolas). Different because: the right side has dx + dy, so the conic is a hyperbola, not a parabola; web search found only the different textbook equations.

concept_use.Polar substitution technique: The combination x dx + y dy is r dr in polar coordinates, which reduces the equation to dr = dx + dy and gives r = x + y - 10.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and function introduced with its domain, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; domain x > 10 stated; the branch with x + y - 10 > 0 is the one through (15,20); answer 110 is a positive 3-digit integer as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: x dx + y dy = r dr, so dr = dx + dy and r = x + y - 10.
justification: One polar identity and an algebraic simplification to a hyperbola; routine once r dr is seen. Comparable to 2025-P2-Q9 (L2).
